reading.body:
Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 1 publishes 5.3 MW of critical load UPS capacity across an 85,388-square-foot facility in Hillsboro, Oregon. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this IT load would support roughly 130 racks. The campus holds certifications for compliance workloads including PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53, which qualify it for regulated enterprise and government applications rather than hyperscale AI training.

This facility ranks seventh by published megawatts in Oregon, accounting for 3.4 percent of the state's 156.6 MW of published data center capacity. Oregon has 133 mapped facilities but only eight publish power figures, making the state's true infrastructure scale opaque. Hillsboro 1 is one of the few campuses in the state with a disclosed electrical footprint.

The campus does not meet the power density or scale required for leading-edge AI model training, which typically demands hundreds of megawatts per site. Its published certifications and customer compliance focus suggest it serves mid-market enterprise and regulated applications. For AI workload assessment, the facility's relevance lies in serving inference, edge processing, or non-training ML applications where power density is lower and compliance requirements are binding.
